anomaly_def.Name: Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly + Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly : Concurrent transactions hold or request incompatible locks on the same resources, causing wait chains or deadlocks that stall or abort statements.
MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly : Obsolete row versions and rollback records accumulate faster than background cleaners can reclaim them, enlarging data structures and slowing visibility checks.
Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly : Database processes hit kernel-enforced ceilings for file descriptors, shared-memory segments, semaphores, threads, or other OS objects, preventing further allocations.

When all three root causes strike together, the database experiences compound symptoms: long lock-wait times and deadlock retries surface alongside rapidly growing version stores, bloated tables, and constantly busy autovacuum/cleaner tasks. Simultaneously, background workers, parallel query helpers, or even ordinary sessions intermittently fail to start because the process exhausts file-handle, semaphore, or shared-memory limits. Administrators see lock-manager wait graphs, surging deadlock victim counts, soaring disk usage from version bloat, cleanup workers stuck or throttled, and operating-system logs complaining about resource exhaustion. From the client side this manifests as unpredictable latency spikes, timeouts, aborted transactions that must be retried, and sporadic "cannot allocate OS resource" errors.

Causal chain: heavy OLTP update/delete activity creates many row versions; long-running or blocked transactions (due to lock contention) keep old snapshots alive, preventing version cleanup and inflating the version store. The swelling version store enlarges on-disk structures and lengthens checkpoint and vacuum cycles, which in turn extend lock durations and increase contention. To cope, the database spawns more cleanup or parallel worker processes—quickly approaching or exceeding OS limits on file descriptors, shared memory, or process counts. Once those limits are hit, new workers cannot start, further stalling vacuum and deadlock-detector activity, so both version bloat and lock queues worsen. Each anomaly therefore reinforces the others, driving a feedback loop that degrades throughput and may culminate in partial or full service outage.

entry.official_definition: Terminates any session that has been idle within an open transaction for longer than the specified amount of time.
entry.trigger_condition: A session is idle, waiting for a client query, while an open transaction remains active longer than the configured threshold.
entry.workload_impact: The session is terminated; this prevents long idle transactions from holding locks or preventing vacuum cleanup.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
